title: TTT hidden linear model with Mirror-structured writable state
hypothesis: A shared bank of low-rank writable output subspaces plus one compact code per stream can retain long-context online adaptation quality while reducing recurrent hidden-model state bytes versus full TTT-Linear; mismatched or private directions expose the capacity boundary.
physical_object: Shared 16x16 TTT initialization and 4 rank-4 output bases
mirror_coordinate: Per-stream code selecting a writable rank-4 hidden-update subspace

task.metric: Prequential Gaussian NLL and MSE at all tokens and final 32-token window; actual serialized hidden state bytes; update MAC proxy

controls: Full TTT-Linear writable 16x16 matrix per stream
One fixed rank-4 writable basis shared by every stream
Independent rank-4 TTT state with a private basis per stream
Mirror shared rank-4 basis dictionary and per-stream codes
Native shared dictionary with ordinary mode IDs and identical decoder
compute: dense and projected update MAC proxy
success_gate: At both development seeds, Mirror final-window NLL <=1.10x full TTT-Linear and total state payload <=50% of full TTT-Linear; mean all-token NLL <=1.10x independent rank-4 TTT. Strict Mirror-specific gain over native dictionary IDs is also required.
failure_gate: Mirror misses quality/bytes or exactly aliases native dictionary-ID control. Keep fresh seeds sealed on failure.
boundaries: Synthetic supervised online linear regression, TTT-like writable state only
No reproduction of self-supervised TTT-Linear/TTT-MLP paper results
Task-family output bases are generated and charged; no hidden free basis
